title: Small and Large Dust Cavities in Disks around Mid-M Stars in Taurus
question: Do disks around mid-M stars in Taurus show dust substructures (rings and cavities) at ~50 mas resolution, and what could cause them?

evidence.quote: All properties are calculated from distances obtained from inverting the parallax in (cite: gaiadr3).

what.value: Spectral type and extinction for 2M0450 and 2M0508

evidence.quote: For 2M0450 and 2M0508, the spectral type and extinction are obtained from (cite: luhman18)

evidence.loc: 3.4 Millimeter Flux, Dust Disk Mass and Size
evidence.quote: it is consistent with $1.16^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$ mJy reported in (cite: akeson2019)

what.value: SED photometry from GALEX, SDSS, Pan-STARRS, Gaia, 2MASS, WISE, Spitzer, Herschel

evidence.quote: The SED data points are collected from GALEX GR6+7 (cite: bianchi2017), SDSS DR17 (cite: abdurrouf2022), PAN-STARRS (cite: flewelling2020)

external_data.citation: (cite: bianchi2017; abdurrouf2022; flewelling2020; gaia2022; skrutskie2006; wright2010; luhman2010; marton2017)

what.value: Pre-main-sequence evolutionary tracks with 51% spot coverage for masses

evidence.quote: The masses are then estimated using the (cite: somers20) evolutionary tracks for pre-main sequence stars with 51% spots coverage.

recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, flag channels, average to 125 MHz, phase-only self-cal where helpful, tclean multiscale imaging with uv-tapered versions
Fit Gaussian profile (2M0450, CIDA 12) or radially asymmetric Gaussian ring(s) (others) with inclination, PA, offsets; galario for model visibilities
assumptions: Uniform priors; inclination prior ∝ sin i

recipe.goal: Test for hidden small cavities (Nuker) and central emission
recipe.method: Fit Nuker profile to 2M0450 and CIDA 12; compare via BIC; add central point source to 2M0436 ring model
key_parameters: Nuker priors: log10 alpha U(0,2), beta U(0,10), gamma approx uniform (-3,2); point flux U(0,1) mJy

recipe.goal: Derive flux, dust mass, dust sizes
recipe.method: Integrate model intensity for flux and R68/R90; optically thin mass formula
assumptions: Optically thin, T_dust = 20 K, kappa = 2.3 cm2/g (nu/230 GHz)^0.4, Gaia DR3 distances, 10% flux calibration error

recipe.goal: CO fluxes and gas disk sizes
recipe.method: Elliptical extraction regions sized from cumulative flux, with dust inclination and PA; noise from 1000 random regions in line-free channels; gas R90 like dust
assumptions: Gas radii are lower limits due to cloud absorption and resolved-out emission

recipe.goal: SED radiative transfer for micron-grain cavity sizes
recipe.method: RADMC-3D flared disk with BT-Settl star; grid over Rin, beta, H100; p=-1, Rout=R90 mm
key_parameters: beta in [1.0,1.2], H100 in [5,15], Rin between sublimation radius and mm cavity; grains 0.01-1000 um
assumptions: Dust model of Birnstiel et al. 2018; well-mixed gas and dust

evidence.quote: with the inner ring peak at 61.7 au and the outer ring peak at 113.9 au
we find a ring peak at 9.8 au
the best-fit ring peaks at 12.2 au
the best model finds a ring peak at 6.8 au
emission peak at $\sim$ 1.7 au for 2M0450 and 5.7 au for CIDA 12
CIDA 12 has the lowest dust mass with only $0.51^{+0.05}_{-0.05} M_\oplus$
the Gaussian profile gives $0.60^{+0.06}_{-0.06}$ mJy, while the Nuker profile recovers a flux of $1.20^{+0.98}_{-0.51}$ mJy

not_stated_but_needed: Multiscale scales, cell size, image size, masks and clean thresholds
Per-source MCMC priors bounds for ring models
Flux/continuum visibility weighting treatment and reference for ALMA pipeline versions
Exact CO velocity/channel settings for moment maps and extraction radii
SED fit: dust opacity composition details, inclination and photometry values
Time-series check method for flux variability
score_reason: Clear modeling approach with named tools and parameters, but several imaging details absent and code not released.
rediscovery_reason: Data from ALMA project are archival, model equations and MCMC settings are given, and results (ring radii, dust masses, sizes) are numeric.
